polls.pollster: St. Pete Polls for Florida Politics

media.what: Called DSA member Angie Nixon's Democratic Senate primary win the best midterm news for the GOP since Platner.
Gave Laura Loomer Donkey of the Day on The Breakfast Club over her attacks on Democratic Senate nominee Angie Nixon.
Inside Elections moved the Florida Senate race for Ashley Moody's seat from Solid Republican to Likely Republican.

research.summary: Appointed Republican Sen. Ashley Moody faces Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon of Jacksonville in the special election for the rest of Marco Rubio's term, with a Stetson poll showing Moody holding a double digit lead in a state where Republicans have about 1.5 million more registered voters. Moody casts Nixon as a socialist who is soft on crime, while Nixon, who outraised Moody last quarter, attacks Moody over the Hope Florida settlement and health care cuts.

issues.why: Democrats say Moody's office approved a Medicaid settlement that routed 10 million dollars to political committees, while Moody has not been charged and denies wrongdoing.
Moody runs on her record as a judge and attorney general and says Nixon quotes cop killers, which Nixon disputes.
Nixon joined the Democratic Socialists of America in June but calls herself a capitalist who supports regulation, while Moody frames the race as freedom versus socialism.

issues.issue: Cost of living and student debt
issues.why: Nixon focuses on rising costs, student debt and low paying jobs for graduates.
Nixon says Moody voted to end health care for over 440,000 Floridians.

storylines.title: Sanders rallies thousands with Nixon at UF
storylines.what: Bernie Sanders and Nixon drew more than 2,800 people in Gainesville, urging young voters to turn out on costs and student debt.

storylines.title: Nixon outraises Moody
storylines.what: Nixon raised about 2 million dollars more than Moody in the third quarter on a jump in small donors, but still has less cash on hand.

storylines.title: Nixon says Moody should be jailed
storylines.what: In a TV interview Nixon said she wants Moody locked up over Hope Florida and would seek an investigation. Moody's campaign called it a tactic from the communist playbook.

storylines.title: Moody ad touts tough on crime record
storylines.what: A Moody ad says she spent her career putting criminals behind bars and that her opponent quotes cop killers, citing Nixon's past praise of Assata Shakur.

storylines.title: Democrats hit Moody on Hope Florida and access
storylines.what: Florida Democrats accused Moody of dodging reporters and town halls and revived the Hope Florida controversy. Moody declined to debate Nixon, calling her a self proclaimed socialist.

storylines.title: Moody ad labels Nixon a socialist
storylines.what: Moody's ad shows Nixon discussing joining the DSA and frames the race as freedom versus socialism.

storylines.title: Trump endorses Moody
storylines.what: Trump released a video fully endorsing Moody, crediting her tax cut and border votes, and called Nixon a communist.

events.title: The socialist label
events.prompt: Attack ads hammer one candidate's membership in the Democratic Socialists of America. Reporters ask whether the label fits.

opts.label: Own the left lane
opts.say: Embrace a progressive agenda on wages, housing and health care.

opts.label: Capitalist who regulates
opts.say: Say you believe in markets with rules and focus on costs.

opts.label: Freedom versus socialism
opts.say: Frame the race as a choice between freedom and socialism.

events.title: Hope Florida questions
events.prompt: A 10 million dollar Medicaid settlement routed to political committees is back in the news, and reporters ask what should happen.

opts.label: Call for prosecution
opts.say: Say those responsible should be punished and promise an investigation.

opts.label: Demand transparency
opts.say: Call for full release of records and let investigators do their work.

opts.label: Dismiss as smear
opts.say: Note no one was charged and call the attacks a political smear.

events.title: Debate request
events.prompt: One candidate refuses to debate, saying the other does not deserve a platform. The other accuses her of hiding from voters.

opts.label: Hold open town halls
opts.say: Hold town halls across the state and challenge the opponent to show up.

opts.label: One televised debate
opts.say: Agree to a single debate with a mainstream moderator.

opts.label: No platform
opts.say: Decline and say an extreme opponent should not get a stage.

events.title: Policing and public safety
events.prompt: An ad says one candidate quotes cop killers and wants to empty prisons. You need a public safety message.

opts.label: Reform and prevention
opts.say: Call for justice reform and investment in prevention, and reject the ad as false.

opts.label: Fund police and reform
opts.say: Back funding for police along with accountability measures.

opts.label: Lock up criminals
opts.say: Run on a record of putting criminals behind bars and backing law enforcement.

ads.theme: Labels Nixon a socialist and frames the race as freedom versus socialism.
Touts her record putting criminals behind bars and says Nixon quotes cop killers.

regions.name: South Florida
regions.note: The Democratic base in Broward and Palm Beach, while Miami-Dade's Hispanic voters have swung sharply Republican.

regions.name: Orlando and the I 4 east
regions.note: Growing, diverse Orlando metro with a large Puerto Rican community, flanked by Republican Volusia.

regions.name: Tampa Bay
regions.note: The classic swing region, now leaning Republican outside Tampa and St. Petersburg.

regions.name: Northeast Florida
regions.note: Nixon's Jacksonville base is competitive, with Gainesville Democratic and the suburbs strongly Republican.

regions.name: Southwest Gulf Coast
regions.note: Retiree heavy and among the most Republican areas of the state.

regions.name: Panhandle and Big Bend
regions.note: Military heavy Deep South politics, with Democratic Tallahassee in Leon.
